global_briefing: Keep three world events in view. The Trump–Xi talks at APEC in Shenzhen, reportedly in a three-way format with Putin, put trade on the table in the same week as the desk's test of China's antimony, tungsten and rare-earth licence terms, so expect trade-stability framing with minerals detail later, if at all. The Ukraine war keeps munitions demand high, which sustains the defence money flowing to tungsten and antimony and would shrink if fighting stopped. Hormuz remains the largest cost risk: a sustained disruption would raise diesel and sulphur costs for leach copper and HPAL nickel before it cut metal output. Mongolia's president's resignation adds policy-delay risk to Oyu Tolgoi.
